raw_text:
Below is a structured 12-week strength + hypertrophy program beginning 2026-06-01. It’s designed for a healthy, recreationally trained 26-year-old female on a combined oral contraceptive (no cycle-phasing needed). The goal is strength and body composition: progressive overload on compound lifts, sufficient hypertrophy volume, and nutritional/recovery guidance to support performance and recomposition.

Overview
- Duration: 12 weeks (2026-06-01 to 2026-08-23)
- Frequency: 4 lifting days/week + 1–2 short conditioning sessions + daily low-intensity movement
- Split: Upper/Lower emphasis with strength focus early in the week, hypertrophy/volume later
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Base/accumulation — technique, volume base
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Intensification — heavier loads, moderate volume
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength-hypertrophy — undulating rep schemes
  - Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak/consolidation — strength focus, strategic deload in Week 12

Weekly Structure (Mon–Sun template)
- Mon: Lower A (Strength-leaning)
- Tue: Upper A (Strength-leaning)
- Wed: Optional LISS 20–30 min or rest + mobility
- Thu: Lower B (Hypertrophy-leaning)
- Fri: Upper B (Hypertrophy-leaning)
- Sat: Optional conditioning (10–20 min intervals) + core
- Sun: Rest, steps/mobility

Load Guidance
- RPE or reps in reserve (RIR) noted; adjust loads to stay in the target effort.
- Progression: if completing top-end reps at target RIR, increase load next week by 2.5–5 kg for lower body compounds, 1–2.5 kg for upper.

Warm-Up (each session)
- 5–8 min light cardio + dynamic mobility (hips, T-spine, shoulders)
- Specific warm-up: 2–4 ascending sets for first main lift (e.g., 5–3–2 reps)

Core/Mobility Finishers
- Rotate anti-extension (dead bug, ab wheel), anti-rotation (pallof press), and carries.

Conditioning
- LISS: 20–30 min brisk walk, incline treadmill, bike, or easy row (Zone 2).
- Intervals: 6–10 rounds of 30s hard/90s easy (bike/rower/assault) at RPE 8–9.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 (Base/Accumulation)
Goal: Build movement quality and a volume base. Moderate loads, 2–3 RIR.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 to 06-07)
- Mon Lower A
  - Back Squat 4x6 @ RPE 7 (2–3 RIR)
  - Romanian Deadlift 3x8 @ RPE 7
  - Walking Lunge 3x10/side
  - Leg Curl (machine) 3x12
  - Standing Calf Raise 3x12–15
  - Core: Dead Bug 3x8/side
- Tue Upper A
  - Bench Press (barbell) 4x6 @ RPE 7
  - Pendlay Row 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
  - Seated DB Shoulder Press 3x8
  - Lat Pulldown (wide or neutral) 3x10
  - Incline DB Fly 2x12
  - Triceps Rope Pressdown 2x12
  - Core: Pallof Press 3x10/side
- Thu Lower B
  - Conventional Deadlift 4x5 @ RPE 7
  - Front Squat 3x6–8 @ RPE 7
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8/side
  - Hip Thrust 3x10
  - Seated Calf Raise 3x12–15
  - Core: Side Plank 3x30–45s/side
- Fri Upper B
  - Overhead Press (barbell) 4x5–6 @ RPE 7
  - One-Arm DB Row 3x10/side
  - Close-Grip Bench Press 3x8
  - Cable Row (neutral) 3x10–12
  - Lateral Raise 3x12–15
  - EZ-Bar Curl 3x10–12
  - Core: Ab Wheel or Stability Ball Rollout 3x8–10
- Conditioning: Wed LISS 20–30 min; Sat optional intervals 6x30/90

Week 2
- Keep exercises; add 2.5–5 kg lower body and 1–2.5 kg upper where reps/RIR were met.
- Increase one accessory set for quads and back:
  - Add 1 set to Front Squat (now 4x6–8) and Lat Pulldown (now 4x10).
- Maintain same RPE targets.

Week 3
- Progress loads similarly.
- Slight rep progression on compounds:
  - Back Squat 5x5 @ RPE 7–8 (2 RIR)
  - Bench Press 5x5 @ RPE 7–8
  - Deadlift 5x4 @ RPE 7–8
  - OHP 5x4–5 @ RPE 7–8
- Keep accessory volume stable; aim to reach top-end reps.

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 (Intensification)
Goal: Heavier work on main lifts, moderate accessory volume. 1–2 RIR.

Week 4
- Mon Lower A
  - Back Squat 5x4 @ RPE 8 (1–2 RIR)
  - RDL 4x6 @ RPE 8
  - Hack Squat or Leg Press 3x10
  - Leg Curl 3x10–12
  - Standing Calf Raise 3x12–15
  - Core: Hanging Knee Raise 3x10–12
- Tue Upper A
  - Bench Press 5x4 @ RPE 8
  - Bent-Over Row (barbell) 4x6 @ RPE 8
  - Seated DB Press 3x6–8
  - Weighted Pull-Up or Assisted 4x5–6 (or Cable Pulldown 4x8)
  - Cable Fly 2x12
  - Skullcrusher 3x10
  - Core: Pallof Press 3x12/side
- Thu Lower B
  - Deadlift 5x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - Front Squat 4x5–6 @ RPE 8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 3x8–10/side
  - Hip Thrust 3x8–10 (2s pause at top)
  - Seated Calf Raise 3x12–15
  - Core: Side Plank Hip Lift 3x10/side
- Fri Upper B
  - Overhead Press 5x3–4 @ RPE 8
  - One-Arm Chest-Supported Row 4x8/side
  - Close-Grip Bench 3x6–8
  - Lat Pulldown (neutral) 3x10
  - Lateral Raise 3x12–15 (last set drop set optional)
  - Cable Curl 3x10–12
  - Core: Ab Wheel 3x8–10
- Conditioning: Wed LISS; Sat intervals 7–8 rounds

Week 5
- Progress loads 1–3%.
- Main lift top sets + back-off:
  - Back Squat: Top single @ RPE 7–8, then 4x4 @ RPE 8
  - Bench: Top single @ RPE 7–8, then 4x4 @ RPE 8
  - Deadlift: Top single @ RPE 7–8, then 4x3 @ RPE 8
  - OHP: Top single @ RPE 7–8, then 4x3 @ RPE 8
- Keep accessories same; push to near top reps.

Week 6
- Maintain structure; increase back-off loads slightly if RIR permits.
- Slight volume drop on accessories (remove 1 set from one quad and one push accessory) to emphasize recovery.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 (Strength-Hypertrophy Undulating)
Goal: Alternate rep ranges across the week; maintain high-quality volume. 1–2 RIR.

Week 7
- Mon Lower A (Strength)
  - Back Squat 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 4x5–6 @ RPE 8
  - Leg Press 3x8
  - Hamstring Curl 3x10
  - Standing Calf 3x12–15
  - Core: Hanging Leg Raise 3x10–12
- Tue Upper A (Strength)
  - Bench Press 5x3 @ RPE 8
  - Barbell Row 4x5–6 @ RPE 8
  - DB Shoulder Press 3x6–8
  - Weighted Pull-Up 4x4–6
  - Dips or CGBP 2–3x6–8
  - Face Pull 2x12–15
  - Core: Pallof Press 3x12/side
- Thu Lower B (Hypertrophy)
  - Deadlift 4x4 @ RPE 8
  - Front Squat 4x6–8
  - Split Squat (long stride) 3x10/side
  - Hip Thrust 3x10–12
  - Seated Calf 3x12–15
  - Core: Copenhagen Plank 3x20–30s/side
- Fri Upper B (Hypertrophy)
  - OHP 4x4 @ RPE 8
  - Chest-Supported Row 4x8–10
  - Incline DB Bench 3x8–10
  - Pulldown (neutral) 3x10–12
  - Lateral Raise 3x15
  - Curl + Pressdown superset 2–3x12 each
  - Core: Ab Wheel 3x8–10
- Conditioning: 1 LISS + 1 intervals (8–9 rounds)

Week 8
- Progress loads where reps/RIR allow.
- Introduce one higher-rep metabolite set per body part (last set):
  - Quads: Leg Press last set 15–20 reps @ 1–2 RIR
  - Back: Row last set 12–15 reps
  - Delts: Lateral raise 20–25 reps
- Keep main lift reps same; aim for +2.5 kg lower, +1–2.5 kg upper if bar speed solid.

Week 9
- Slight intensity push on main lifts:
  - Squat 4x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
  - Bench 4x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
  - Deadlift 4x3–4 @ RPE 8–8.5
  - OHP 4x3 @ RPE 8–8.5
- Reduce accessories by 1 set for quads and chest this week to manage fatigue.

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 (Peak/Consolidation + Deload)
Goal: Leverage prior work for strength expression and quality hypertrophy stimulus, then deload/test.

Week 10
- Mon Lower A
  - Back Squat: Top single @ RPE 8, then 3x3 @ RPE 8
  - RDL 3x5–6
  - Leg Press 2–3x8–10
  - Ham Curl 2–3x10–12
  - Calf 2–3x12–15
  - Core: Hanging Leg Raise 3x8–10
- Tue Upper A
  - Bench: Top single @ RPE 8, then 3x3 @ RPE 8
  - Barbell Row 3x5–6
  - DB Shoulder Press 2–3x6–8
  - Pull-Up/Pulldown 3x6–8
  - Triceps Pressdown 2x10–12
  - Core: Pallof 3x10–12/side
- Thu Lower B
  - Deadlift: Top single @ RPE 8, then 3x2–3 @ RPE 8
  - Front Squat 3x4–6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat 2x8–10/side
  - Hip Thrust 2x8–10
  - Calf 2–3x12–15
  - Core: Side Plank 3x30–45s/side
- Fri Upper B
  - OHP: Top single @ RPE 8, then 3x2–3 @ RPE 8
  - Chest-Supported Row 3x8
  - Incline DB Bench 2–3x6–8
  - Pulldown 2–3x8–10
  - Lateral Raise 2x12–15
  - Curl 2x10–12
  - Core: Ab Wheel 3x8
- Conditioning: Optional only if recovery is strong; keep low (1 LISS, skip intervals if heavy fatigue).

Week 11
- Slight load bump on back-off sets if last week felt submaximal (still 1–2 RIR).
- Keep volume similar or -1 set per accessory if fatigue accumulates.
- Emphasize bar speed; no grinders.

Week 12 (Deload/Test and Assess)
Option A: Deload (recommended if signs of fatigue)
- All main lifts: 3x3 @ ~60–65% 1RM (RPE 5–6)
- Accessories: 1–2 sets each @ RPE 6–7, cut metabolite work
- Conditioning: LISS only 1–2x 20 min
Option B: Performance check (if feeling great)
- Squat/Bench/Deadlift/OHP: Work to a smooth single @ RPE 8–8.5; then 2x2 @ ~80% of that single
- Minimal accessories (1–2 sets each, easy)
- Record estimated 1RMs and body metrics

Progression & Autoregulation Notes
- If a set hits prescribed reps with 2 RIR or better and bar speed is stable, increase load next session.
- If you miss reps or RPE drifts >0.5 above target, hold load or reduce 2.5–5%.
- Use double progression on accessories: add reps until top of the range, then add load.

Nutrition (for strength + body recomposition)
- Calorie target: slight deficit to maintenance if body fat loss is a priority; otherwise small surplus for strength.
  - Start point: 30–35 kcal/kg/day as maintenance estimate; adjust by +/− 200–300 kcal based on weekly scale trend (aim −0.25–0.5% bodyweight/week if cutting).
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 3–5 meals. Include 25–40 g high-quality protein within 1–2 h post-training.
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day; bias more carbs around workouts (pre: 30–60 g, post: 60–90 g depending on session size).
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Since she’s on COC, maintain adequate dietary fat for general health; no cycle phasing required.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add 500–1000 ml around training. Sodium 3–5 g/day (unless medically contraindicated) to support performance in heat.
- Micronutrients: Ensure iron, calcium (1000 mg/day), vitamin D3 (1000–2000 IU/day if levels unknown), omega-3 (1–2 g EPA/DHA).

Recovery & Lifestyle
- Sleep: 7–9 h/night; consistent schedule.
- Steps: 7–10k/day, primarily low-intensity NEAT to aid recomposition.
- Mobility: 8–12 min post-session or on rest days (hips, T-spine, shoulders, ankles).
- Stress: 5–10 min daily breath work or relaxation.
- Deload indicators: persistent soreness, declining bar speed, poor sleep, elevated RPEs — consider earlier volume reduction.

Monitoring
- Weekly: body weight (3–4x/week average), progress photos, performance log (loads/RPEs), subjective recovery (sleep, stress).
- Adjustments after Week 3 and Week 6: 
  - If not progressing on compounds, reduce accessory volume by 2–4 sets/week and add 1 extra rest day or replace one interval with LISS.
  - If recovery excellent and reps feel easy, add 1 set to one major accessory per session and/or increase interval rounds by 1.

Exercise Substitutions (equipment or preference)
- Squat: back squat → safety bar squat or high-bar; front squat → goblet or hack squat.
- Deadlift: conventional → trap bar or sumo.
- Bench: barbell → DB flat or machine press.
- OHP: barbell → DB seated or Arnold press.
- Rows: barbell → chest-supported, cable, or seal row.
- Pull-Ups: assisted machine or pulldown variants.

Notes specific to COC users
- No need to phase training around withdrawal bleeds given asymptomatic profile.
- Maintain adequate iron and calcium; monitor hydration and temperature tolerance in hot weather.

This plan gives you week-by-week structure with clear progression, plus nutrition and recovery to support both strength and favorable body composition over 12 weeks. Adjust loads via RPE/RIR and make small nutritional tweaks based on weekly outcomes.
